quote.citation: 1704, John Dunton, The Athenian Oracle, Athenian Society, Volume III, page 67,
quote.text: […] and indeed it seems a Hardſhip in our Laws, that a poor Shoplift ſhou′d be hang′d for breaking in and pilfering a few Goods, […] .

definitions.definition: (transitive) To steal something from a shop or store during business hours, usually by means of hiding merchandise.

quote.citation: 2004 May 17, Andrew Sean Greer, The New Yorker:
quote.text: She taught Maddy to sing in Portuguese, to shoplift mascara, to play a drinking game called Spoons

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To steal from shops / stores during trading hours.

quote.citation: 1938 April, William Peery, “Thank Rotary!”, in The Rotarian, page 52:
quote.text: Once, before we had juvenile court here, I made the mistake of putting on probation a boy who had shoplifted, a boy of good family. That boy later shot a man.

quote.citation: 1969 October, Gwendolyn Midlo Hall, Mechanisms for Exploiting the Black Community, Negro Digest, 22,
quote.text: Thus, the teacher shook down the kids, the big kids shook down the little kids, the little kids shoplifted to get money, etc., etc.
In other words, New York is a better place to shoplift.
